title: The Renaissance and the Reformation
note: The Renaissance (c. 1350 to 1600) began in the wealthy city-states of Italy as a revival of classical learning called humanism. The printing press spread its ideas. In 1517 Martin Luther's protest against indulgences began the Protestant Reformation, which permanently divided Western Christianity.

read.title: New learning, divided faith
text: In the 1300s and 1400s, Italian cities such as Florence grew rich from banking and trade. Wealthy families like the Medici paid artists and scholars to glorify their cities. Humanists such as Petrarch searched monasteries for lost Latin and Greek texts and urged the study of grammar, history, poetry and ethics. Artists studied ancient sculpture and used perspective to make paintings seem real. This revival is called the Renaissance, or rebirth.

Around 1450 Johannes Gutenberg developed printing with movable metal type. Books became cheaper and more plentiful, and ideas could spread across Europe in weeks. Northern humanists such as Erasmus used the new tool to publish better editions of the Bible and to criticize abuses in the church.

In 1517 Martin Luther, a monk and professor in Wittenberg, challenged the sale of indulgences. He taught that salvation came through faith alone and that the Bible, not the pope, was the final authority. Printed copies of his writings spread rapidly. Some German princes protected him, and other reformers, such as John Calvin in Geneva, founded their own churches. In England, Henry VIII broke with Rome for political and personal reasons. The Catholic Church answered with the Council of Trent and new orders such as the Jesuits. Religious wars followed, ending in Germany only with the Peace of Westphalia in 1648.
